title: Iron Pillar of Delhi
summary: The Iron Pillar of Delhi stands in the Qutb Minar complex. A metallurgical study by R. Balasubramaniam of IIT Kanpur attributes its construction to Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (AD 376-414) and says it was brought to Delhi in the 11th century.

uncertainty.note: Dated to the reign of Chandragupta II as given by Balasubramaniam (AD 376-414).

where.modern_name: Iron Pillar, Qutb complex, Mehrauli, Delhi, India
where.historical_name: Iron pillar, originally at Udayagiri per Balasubramaniam, Gupta Empire; moved to Delhi in the 11th century

importance.justification: Famous for its corrosion resistance and early Indian iron-making.

sources.title: On the corrosion resistance of the Delhi iron pillar
sources.author: R. Balasubramaniam

sources.title: Qutb Minar and its Monuments, Delhi
sources.author: UNESCO

reviewer_note: Date is the king's reign: the inscription names Chandra, identified as Chandragupta II (probable, not certain). No model: the dimensions found (7.2 m total, 41-42 cm diameter) are on journalism pages only, and the Balasubramaniam paper I opened gives none. Pin is Wikidata; UNESCO Qutb property point is 28 31 32.988 N, 77 11 7.008 E.
